## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

head(economics)

# Exercise 7

The economics dataset contains:

- **date** - Date
- **pce** - Personal consumption expenditures
- **pop** - Population
- **psavert** - Personal savings rate
- **uempmed** - Median unemployment duration
- **unemploy** - Number of unemployed people

> Create a scatter plot.

```{r}
plot <- ggplot(
  economics,
  aes(x = unemploy,
      y = uempmed)
) +
  geom_point()

plot +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship between Unemployment and Median Duration",
    x = "Number of Unemployed",
    y = "Median Duration of Unemployment"
  )
```

# Exercise 8

```{r}
#| label: fig-unemployment
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between unemployment and duration."
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-asp: 0.6

economics |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = unemploy,
      y = uempmed
    )
  ) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship between Unemployment and Duration",
    x = "Number of Unemployed",
    y = "Median Duration"
  )
```

# Exercise 9

::: callout-note
The scatter plot in @fig-unemployment suggests that higher unemployment levels tend to coincide with longer median unemployment durations. While the relationship is not perfectly linear, there appears to be a positive association.
:::
